In the control of acute mania lithium is often too slow in onset to be used alone and therefore additional therapy with an antipsychotic may be necessary. It should be noted, however, that such combinations should be used with care as interactions and adverse reactions have occurred. The renal excretion of lithium is increased by chlorpromazine treatment,1 which means that subsequent withdrawal of chlor- promazine can result in an abrupt rise in serum-lithium concen- trations.2 The serum concentration of chlorpromazine can also be reduced by lithium,3 and chlorpromazine toxicity may be precip- itated by the abrupt withdrawal of lithium in patients previously stabilised on both drugs. Ventricular fibrillation has been de- scribed after withdrawal of lithium in a patient also taking chlor- promazine;4 it was suggested that the chlorpromazine dose should be reduced if lithium is to be stopped.
